### J-7 `start --empty` overwrites docs the dev already wrote
- quote: "when they don't exist (FR-12)"
- quote: "(d / f"{n}.md").write_text("
- situation (adversary): the dev confirmed `stack.md` by hand, or a run is resumed. Someone runs `nio onboard start --empty` again, which is allowed from `in progress`, `skipped` and `done`. The code writes every doc in `DOCS`, all six rather than only `stack`, `architecture` and `infra`. It writes them unconditionally, so confirmed docs become `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` stubs with no backup and no message. `products.md` and `personas.md` are lost too. The spec said to write them only when they don't exist.
- situation (correctness): `.nio/project/stack.md` already holds confirmed content and the dev runs `start --empty`. The code overwrites it with blank sections, which is data loss. It does this for all six DOCS, including `product`, `personas` and `principles`, which FR-12 says are still grilled. The generated sections come from the invented `SECTIONS` map, not the CT-12 `HEADINGS`.
- situation (consistency): a repo that is in progress with stack.md already confirmed. `nio onboard start --empty` rewrites every one of the six docs with NEEDS CLARIFICATION. The write has no exists check, and the table's in-progress row says start is ignored there. The code also writes product, personas and principles, which CT-4 leaves out. The stack.md it writes has `## Frameworks` where CT-12 names `Dependencies` and `Commands`, so the template check fails when the doc is confirmed.
- fix: write a doc only if the file is absent, and only the three CT-4 names.
- validation: confirmed: onboard.py line 93-94 loops over all six DOCS and calls write_text with no exists check. CT-4 and FR-12 limit this to stack, architecture and infra, and only when they don't exist.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-36

### J-8 `start` and `skip` on a finished onboarding silently reopen or erase it
- quote: "start on `done` → `onboarding is done; it runs once: use @nio:reconcile-onboarding`"
- quote: "skip on `done` → `onboarding is done already`"
- situation (adversary): onboarding is `done`. `nio onboard start` takes the `st["state"] = "in progress"` branch, which has no `done` check. Done is reopened and `--empty` overwrites docs (F1). `nio onboard skip x` sets `skipped` and loses `done`, so `seen` and the freshness baseline become meaningless. `start` on `in progress` also does not print `ignored`. The test `test_empty_start_writes_blank_docs` and the others never hit the `done` row.
- situation (correctness): onboarding is `done` and the dev runs `nio onboard skip "x"`. The code sets the state to `skipped` and prints `skipped`. CT-4 requires exit 1 with `onboarding is done already`. A completed onboarding is lost, and `nio status` then reports `skipped`. Skip on `skipped` is also not an `ignored: onboarding is skipped` no-op.
- situation (security): `act` runs `(d / f"{n}.md").write_text(...)` for all six DOCS with no existence check. A dev who has confirmed `stack.md` and `infra.md` runs `nio onboard start --empty`, or is on a repo that already has `.nio/project/` docs. The files are replaced with blank templates and the confirmed content is lost. This also writes `product`, `personas` and `principles`, which the contract does not list, and the same overwrite happens on a start after `skipped`. Nothing backs up the files, and FR-29 says a backup copy is made before NIO changes a file.
- fix: add the table's reject and ignore cells per state before acting.
- validation: merged: same as J-19

### J-9 `pause` and `confirm` ignore the state table, so a wrong order corrupts state
- quote: "pause outside `in progress`"
- quote: "st["confirmed"] = sorted(set(st["confirmed"]) | {doc})"
- situation (adversary): `pause` from `not started`, `done` or `skipped` sets `paused` (`st["state"] = "paused"`). A finished or deliberately skipped project then blocks every full and epic spec, because `spec.new` refuses `paused`. The CT-4 `ignore` cells should have printed `ignored` and changed nothing. `confirm` from `not started`, `skipped` or `done` adds to `confirmed` without changing state. A `confirm` from `done` can mutate the saved set after the freshness baseline was taken.
- situation (correctness): `pause` on `done` or `not started` sets the state to `paused`; `pause` on `done` reopens a finished onboarding and then blocks specs. `confirm` on `not started` records a doc as confirmed. `confirm` never checks that the doc file exists or passes the check_doc test, and never moves the state to `done` or saves `seen`. It prints `done` while the state stays `in progress`, so `spec.new` still refuses. `test_empty_start_writes_blank_docs` asserts `confirm stack` exits 1 in `paused`, which contradicts the ignore cell, so the test locks in the defect.
- fix: gate on `st["state"] == "in progress"` for pause and confirm, otherwise print `ignored: onboarding is <state>`.
- validation: merged: same as J-19

### J-10 `confirm` accepts any doc with no file and never reaches `done` for `--empty`
- quote: "confirm in `in progress` when the doc file `.nio/project/[<app>/]<doc>.md` is missing or fails CT-12's check"
- quote: "rest = [n for n in DOCS if n not in st["confirmed"]]"
- situation (adversary): an agent or dev runs `nio onboard confirm infra` with no `infra.md`. It is recorded as confirmed with no check, and `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` stubs can be confirmed too. A later `@nio:onboard` resume then skips the doc, so a never-written doc counts as onboarded and agents' packs lack it. With `--empty` the state is never moved to `done`: `rest` always lists all six docs. `done` is also never saved, and `seen` is never saved. `--app` is not accepted at all, so unknown flags give an argparse usage error.
- situation (adversary): with `done` stored, `start` sets `in progress` again, `skip` sets `skipped`, and `pause` sets `paused`. Each one silently erases the finished onboarding and the reconcile path. `pause` on `not started` or `skipped` flips the state. `confirm` on `not started` or `skipped` records a doc and only prints `next:`. `confirm` also never checks that the doc file exists or passes CT-12, so an unwritten doc can be confirmed. `start` on `paused` raises "onboarding is paused", though CT-4 says a later start from `paused` resumes and keeps the saved `confirmed`. Only `pause` on `paused` follows the table.
- situation (correctness): CT-4 says confirm outside `in progress` is ignored. It also says confirm needs the doc file to exist and pass `check_doc`. The code confirms any doc in any state except paused, even `not started`, `skipped` or `done`. It never moves the state to `done` when the last doc is confirmed, and it saves no `seen`. Without those two steps nothing ever reaches `done`, so a full or epic spec stays refused after a complete onboarding. The code also does not write the progress file atomically (`f.write_text`), as CT-3 specifies.
- fix: check that the file exists and passes the CT-12 `check_doc`, and use an `expected()` list.
- validation: confirmed: Confirm (lines 97-102) only checks `doc in DOCS`, never the file or CT-12. `rest` walks all six DOCS, so `--empty` never ends in `done`. `done` is never saved. cli.py passes no `--app`.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-37

### J-11 The progress file is written non-atomically, and one bad file crashes `nio status`
- quote: "`save(root, p)` writes a temp file next to it and `os.replace`s it"
- quote: "print("\n".join(query.status(root) + onboard.status_lines(root)))"
- situation (adversary): `f.write_text(json.dumps(st))` truncates the file in place. A crash, a kill or two concurrent `confirm` runs leave torn JSON. Two parallel runs also lose one update (read, modify, write). Afterwards `spec.new` and `act` refuse with a clear message, but `nio status` calls `status_lines` outside any `try`. `progress` raises `ValueError`, so the whole status, including the index lines, ends in a traceback. Valid JSON of the wrong shape (`[]`, or a missing key like `confirmed`) raises an uncaught `TypeError` or `KeyError` in all paths. A skip reason containing a newline can also forge extra lines in `nio status` output.
- situation (adversary): 
- fix: write a temp file and `os.replace`. Catch `ValueError` in the `status` branch and print the error line. Validate the loaded shape.
- validation: confirmed: `save` is `f.write_text(json.dumps(st))` (line 74), not temp plus os.replace as CT-3 requires. cli.py line 370 calls `onboard.status_lines` with no try, and `progress` raises ValueError on bad JSON.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-38

### J-13 Start refuses on paused and restarts on done or in progress
- quote: "a later start from `paused` or `skipped` keeps the saved `confirmed`, `empty` and `apps` and ignores new flags"
- quote: "`raise ValueError("onboarding is paused")`"
- situation (correctness): the dev pauses onboarding and later runs `nio onboard start` to resume. The code hits the `paused` guard and exits 1, so a paused onboarding can never resume. The same early guard also rejects `confirm` in `paused`, where CT-4 says it should print `ignored` and exit 0. `start` on `done` moves the state back to `in progress`, where CT-4 says `onboarding is done; it runs once: use @nio:reconcile-onboarding`. `start` on `in progress` re-runs and, with `--empty`, rewrites docs, where CT-4 says it should be ignored.
- situation (security): `act` has no `done` state guard. `skip "x"` on a finished onboarding sets `skipped` and overwrites the recorded state, so the "runs once" rule is gone. `start` on `done` sets `in progress` again, and with `--empty` it overwrites the confirmed docs (see F1). Any dev can undo a completed onboarding without going through reconcile. The same function lets `confirm` move a `not started` or `skipped` run forward without a `start`.
- fix: key `start` on the current state per the CT-4 table: resume from `paused` or `skipped`, reject on `done`, ignore on `in progress`. Do not apply the paused guard to `start`.
- validation: merged: same as J-19

### J-15 Progress file is written non-atomically
- quote: "`save(root, p)` writes a temp file next to it and `os.replace`s it, as `flow.record` does"
- quote: "`f.write_text(json.dumps(st))`"

### J-16 The progress file is written non-atomically and `confirm` skips the doc check
- quote: "`save(root, p)` writes a temp file next to it and `os.replace`s it, as `flow.record` does."
- situation (security): `save()` calls `f.write_text(json.dumps(st))` directly. A crash or kill mid-write leaves a torn `onboarding.json`. `progress` then raises on every later `start`, `nio status` and full or epic `nio new spec`, so the dev is locked out until they repair the file by hand. In the same function, `confirm` never runs `check_doc` or checks that the doc file exists, as CT-4 requires. A dev or agent can therefore mark a doc confirmed that was never written or approved.
- fix: write a temp file next to `onboarding.json` and `os.replace` it. Make `confirm` refuse when the doc file is missing or `check_doc` fails.
